story_overview.user_story: As a user, I want Annie to respect my boundaries and not spam me, so that proactive messages remain helpful rather than annoying.
story_overview.description:
Implement a "subconscious gate" that acts as a spam prevention layer before proactive messages are sent to users. The gate checks multiple conditions (recent contact, daily limits, quiet hours, user preferences) and blocks messages that would be annoying or inappropriate timing.
This gate is called by the wake-up worker BEFORE executing the wake-up agent, ensuring that even if a trigger fires, we respect user boundaries.

criterion.title: Recent Contact Check
criterion.then: - Blocks if user messaged < 1 hour ago - Returns GateResult(allowed=False, reason="recent_contact")

criterion.title: Daily Limit Check
criterion.then: - Tracks count in Redis: proactive:{user_id}:daily:{date} - TTL: 24 hours - Blocks if count >= 5 - Returns GateResult(allowed=False, reason="daily_limit")

criterion.title: Quiet Hours Check
criterion.then: - Checks user's local time - Blocks if 22:00 - 08:00 - Returns GateResult(allowed=False, reason="quiet_hours", defer_until=...)

criterion.title: User Opt-Out Check
criterion.then: - Checks proactive_enabled in user profile - Blocks if explicitly disabled - Returns GateResult(allowed=False, reason="user_opt_out")

criterion.title: Gate Result Model
criterion.then: Returns GateResult with: - allowed: bool - reason: Optional[str] - defer_until: Optional[datetime]

reference.relevance: Primary design documentation for this story. Defines all gate checks, limits, and behavior. Shows Redis key patterns and implementation pseudocode.
reference.key_points: - Recent contact: 1 hour limit - Daily limit: 5 messages per day - Quiet hours: 10 PM - 8 AM (user's local time) - User opt-out: Check proactive_enabled flag - Check order: opt-out → recent contact → daily limit → quiet hours (fail-fast)

pattern.name: Redis Usage Patterns
pattern.example:
# Redis key patterns used in StateManager: # - session:{user_id} - Session data (JSON, TTL: 3600s) # - conversation:{conversation_id} - Message list (JSON array, TTL: 1800s) # - conversation_mapping:{conversation_id} - user_id reverse lookup (TTL: 1800s)
# Pattern: Setting key with TTL await self.redis_client.setex( key, self.SESSION_TTL, json.dumps(session) )
# Pattern: Getting key session_json = await self.redis_client.get(key) if session_json: session = json.loads(session_json)
# Pattern: Error handling try: await self.redis_client.ping() except (redis_exceptions.ConnectionError, redis_exceptions.TimeoutError) as e: logger.error("Redis connection failed", extra={"error": str(e)}) raise RedisConnectionError("Redis server is unreachable", original_error=e)
pattern.key_takeaways: - Use async redis.asyncio as redis - Decode responses with decode_responses=True - Always set TTL when creating keys - Graceful error handling for connection errors - JSON serialize/deserialize for complex data - Use structured logging with extra fields

pattern.name: User Profile Access Patterns
pattern.key_takeaways: - Profile has timezone in basics.timezone field - Use ProfileManager.load_profile_from_cache() for non-blocking reads - Profile preferences can include proactive_enabled flag - Graceful degradation returns empty profile on errors - Cache miss returns empty profile with cached=False

pattern.name: Timezone Handling Patterns
pattern.example:
import pytz from datetime import datetime
# Pattern: Converting to user timezone if basics.get("timezone"): try: user_tz = pytz.timezone(basics['timezone']) user_time = datetime.now(user_tz).strftime("%I:%M %p") basics_lines.append(f"Timezone: {basics['timezone']} (current time: {user_time})") except (pytz.exceptions.UnknownTimeZoneError, ValueError, KeyError) as e: logger.error( f"Failed to convert timezone: {basics.get('timezone')}", extra={"error": str(e), "user_id": user_id} ) # Fallback: just show timezone name basics_lines.append(f"Timezone: {basics['timezone']}")
# Default timezone if not set pacific = pytz.timezone("US/Pacific") timestamp = datetime.now(pacific).isoformat()
pattern.key_takeaways: - Use pytz for timezone conversions - Handle UnknownTimeZoneError gracefully - Default to US/Pacific if timezone not set - Use datetime.now(tz) to get current time in timezone - Log timezone conversion errors for debugging

pattern.name: Session Last Activity Tracking
pattern.example:
# Session structure includes last_activity timestamp session = { "user_id": user_id, "platform": platform, "conversation_id": conversation_id, "created_at": now, "last_activity": now, # ISO 8601 format with Z suffix "message_count": 0 }
# Pattern: Updating last_activity async def update_session_activity(self, user_id: str) -> None: session = await self.get_session(user_id) if not session: return
# Update timestamp session["last_activity"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z") session["message_count"] = session.get("message_count", 0) + 1
# Store with reset TTL await self.redis_client.setex( f"session:{user_id}", self.SESSION_TTL, json.dumps(session) )
# Note: last_activity is in session, NOT a separate key # To get last_activity, you need to read the session first
pattern.key_takeaways: - last_activity is stored INSIDE session:{user_id} JSON - Format: ISO 8601 with Z suffix (e.g., "2025-12-24T10:30:00Z") - Updated every time user sends a message - Parse with datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp.replace('Z', '+00:00')) - Compare timestamps by converting to datetime objects

# Increment on successful send (not on gate check) date_key = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d") counter_key = f"proactive:{user_id}:daily:{date_key}" count = await redis.incr(counter_key) if count == 1: # First increment, set TTL await redis.expire(counter_key, 86400)
# Check during gate current_count = await redis.get(counter_key) if current_count and int(current_count) >= 5: return GateResult(allowed=False, reason="daily_limit")

dataclass_definition.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Optional from datetime import datetime
@dataclass class GateResult: """Result from subconscious gate check.""" allowed: bool reason: Optional[str] = None defer_until: Optional[datetime] = None

class_structure.code:
class SubconsciousGate: """ Spam prevention gate for proactive messages.
Checks multiple conditions before allowing proactive messages: 1. User opt-out - Check proactive_enabled in profile 2. Recent contact - Block if user messaged < 1 hour ago 3. Daily limit - Block if >= 5 proactive messages today 4. Quiet hours - Block if 22:00 - 08:00 in user's timezone
Returns GateResult with allowed flag and optional reason/defer_until. """
# Configuration RECENT_CONTACT_HOURS = 1 DAILY_MESSAGE_LIMIT = 5 QUIET_HOURS_START = 22 # 10 PM QUIET_HOURS_END = 8 # 8 AM
def __init__(self, redis_client: Optional[redis.Redis] = None): """Initialize gate with Redis client.""" # Similar to ProfileManager init pattern
async def check_gate(self, user_id: str) -> GateResult: """Main entry point - run all checks in order.""" # 1. Check opt-out # 2. Check recent contact # 3. Check daily limit # 4. Check quiet hours # Return first blocking result or allowed=True
async def _check_opt_out(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[GateResult]: """Check if user has disabled proactive messages.""" # Use ProfileManager to load profile # Check profile.preferences.proactive_enabled # Return None if allowed, GateResult if blocked
async def _check_recent_contact(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[GateResult]: """Check if user messaged within last hour.""" # Read session:{user_id} # Parse last_activity timestamp # Compare with now
async def _check_daily_limit(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[GateResult]: """Check if daily message limit reached.""" # Read proactive:{user_id}:daily:{date} # Check if count >= 5
async def _check_quiet_hours(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[GateResult]: """Check if current time is in quiet hours.""" # Load profile for timezone # Calculate user's local hour # Check if 22 <= hour or hour < 8 # Calculate defer_until (next 8am)

quiet_hours_defer_calculation.code:
# Calculate defer_until for quiet hours import pytz from datetime import datetime, timedelta
# Get user timezone (default to UTC if not set) user_tz = pytz.timezone(profile.get("basics", {}).get("timezone", "UTC")) user_now = datetime.now(user_tz) user_hour = user_now.hour
if 22 <= user_hour or user_hour < 8: # In quiet hours - calculate next 8am if user_hour >= 22: # After 10pm - defer to 8am tomorrow next_8am = user_now.replace(hour=8, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) next_8am += timedelta(days=1) else: # Before 8am - defer to 8am today next_8am = user_now.replace(hour=8, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
return GateResult( allowed=False, reason="quiet_hours", defer_until=next_8am )

daily_counter_note.important: The daily counter (proactive:{user_id}:daily:{date}) should be incremented ONLY on successful message send, NOT during gate check. The gate only READS the counter. Incrementing happens in the wake-up worker AFTER successful delivery.

notes.note: The daily counter increment happens in Story 13.7 (Arq Background Worker), not in this story. This story only READS the counter during gate checks.
Default behavior is permissive: if profile/session/counter is missing, we ALLOW the message (fail open). Only explicit blocks should prevent sending.
The defer_until field in GateResult is only populated for quiet_hours reason. Other blocking reasons return None for defer_until.
Timezone handling should be defensive: catch all timezone-related exceptions and fall back to UTC if user timezone is invalid or missing.
